key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide metal-ceramic coatings can have their surface roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity tuned by adjusting spraying parameters, with optimal settings maximizing water repellency.
engineering_relevance: The results provide process-parameter rules for designing coating recipes that improve surface functionality in thermal spray applications.
method: Varied detonation spraying parameters, including nozzle passage speed and spray distance.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity/contact angle.
Derived empirical relationships, including inverse power and parabolic laws, to predict surface behavior and identify optimal spraying conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports controlled experimental dependence of roughness, thickness, and contact angle on process conditions and the development of new predictive equations.
watch_item: The relationships appear to be empirical and may require validation across different substrates, nozzle setups, and scaling conditions before broader deployment.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
